# 1. Principles of Reproducible Research

Reproducible research means:
- **Same data + Same code = Same results**
- Others can verify your findings
- You can return to your work months/years later
- Increases transparency and trust in science

Key components:
- Version control
- Documentation
- Data management
- Literate programming
- Environment management

# 2. R Markdown Basics

R Markdown combines narrative text with code to create dynamic documents.

## Creating an R Markdown Document

```{r eval=FALSE}
# In RStudio: File > New File > R Markdown
```

## YAML Header

```yaml
---
title: "My Analysis"
author: "Your Name"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_float: true
    code_folding: hide
    theme: flatly
---
```

## Markdown Syntax

```markdown
# Header 1
## Header 2
### Header 3

**Bold text**
*Italic text*
`Code`

- Bullet point 1
- Bullet point 2

1. Numbered item 1
2. Numbered item 2

[Link text](https://example.com)

![Image caption](path/to/image.png)
```

## Code Chunks

````markdown
```{r chunk-name, echo=TRUE, eval=TRUE}
# R code here
x <- 1:10
mean(x)
```
````

## Chunk Options

```{r eval=FALSE}
# Common options:
# echo = TRUE/FALSE     # Show code
# eval = TRUE/FALSE     # Run code
# include = TRUE/FALSE  # Include output
# warning = TRUE/FALSE  # Show warnings
# message = TRUE/FALSE  # Show messages
# fig.width = 7         # Figure width
# fig.height = 5        # Figure height
# fig.cap = "Caption"   # Figure caption
# cache = TRUE/FALSE    # Cache results
```

## Inline Code

```markdown
The mean is `r mean(1:10)` and the sum is `r sum(1:10)`.
```

The mean is `r mean(1:10)` and the sum is `r sum(1:10)`.

## Output Formats

```yaml
output:
  html_document: default
  pdf_document: default
  word_document: default
  github_document: default
```

## Rendering

```{r eval=FALSE}
# Knit button in RStudio or:
rmarkdown::render("document.Rmd")
rmarkdown::render("document.Rmd", output_format = "pdf_document")
```

# 3. Advanced R Markdown

## Parameters

```yaml
---
title: "Parameterized Report"
params:
  species: "setosa"
  min_sepal_length: 5.0
---
```

```{r eval=FALSE}
# Use parameters
filtered_data <- iris %>%
  filter(Species == params$species,
         Sepal.Length >= params$min_sepal_length)

# Render with parameters
rmarkdown::render("report.Rmd",
                  params = list(species = "virginica",
                                min_sepal_length = 6.0))
```

## Child Documents

```{r child="child_document.Rmd", eval=FALSE}
```

## Conditional Content

```{r results='asis', eval=FALSE}
if (some_condition) {
  cat("## This section appears conditionally\n")
  cat("Content here...\n")
}
```

## Tables

```{r}
# knitr::kable
library(knitr)
kable(head(iris), caption = "First 6 rows of iris dataset")

# kableExtra for more styling
library(kableExtra)
kable(head(iris)) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover")) %>%
  row_spec(0, bold = TRUE, color = "white", background = "#4F81BD")
```

## Tabbed Sections

```markdown
## Results {.tabset}

### Tab 1
Content for tab 1

### Tab 2
Content for tab 2
```

## Mathematical Equations

Inline: $E = mc^2$

Display:
$$\frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$$

# 5. Version Control with Git

## Git Basics

```bash
# Initialize repository
git init

# Check status
git status

# Add files
git add file.R
git add .  # Add all files

# Commit changes
git commit -m "Descriptive commit message"

# View history
git log
git log --oneline

# Create branch
git branch feature-branch
git checkout feature-branch
# Or: git checkout -b feature-branch

# Merge branch
git checkout main
git merge feature-branch

# Push to remote
git push origin main

# Pull from remote
git pull origin main

# Clone repository
git clone https://github.com/user/repo.git
```

## .gitignore

```
# R
.Rhistory
.RData
.Rproj.user/

# Data files (if large)
*.csv
*.rds
data/

# Output
*.html
*.pdf

# OS
.DS_Store
Thumbs.db
```

## GitHub Integration

```bash
# Add remote
git remote add origin https://github.com/username/repository.git

# Push
git push -u origin main

# Create and push branch
git checkout -b new-feature
git push -u origin new-feature

# Pull request (on GitHub website)
```

# 6. Project Organization

## R Projects (.Rproj)

```{r eval=FALSE}
# Create new project in RStudio:
# File > New Project > New Directory > New Project

# Benefits:
# - Sets working directory
# - Isolates environment
# - Easy to switch between projects
```

## Directory Structure

```
project/
├── README.md
├── project.Rproj
├── data/
│   ├── raw/
│   └── processed/
├── scripts/
│   ├── 01_data_cleaning.R
│   ├── 02_analysis.R
│   └── 03_visualization.R
├── notebooks/
│   └── analysis.Rmd
├── output/
│   ├── figures/
│   └── tables/
├── functions/
│   └── my_functions.R
└── docs/
    └── report.Rmd
```

## here Package

```{r}
library(here)

# Automatically finds project root
here()

# Build paths
data_path <- here("data", "raw", "dataset.csv")
output_path <- here("output", "figures", "plot.png")

# Read data
# data <- read.csv(here("data", "raw", "data.csv"))

# Save output
# ggsave(here("output", "figures", "plot.png"))
```

# 7. Dependency Management

## renv Package

```{r eval=FALSE}
# Initialize renv for project
renv::init()

# Install packages (they're tracked in renv.lock)
install.packages("dplyr")

# Take snapshot of current environment
renv::snapshot()

# Restore environment from renv.lock
renv::restore()

# Update packages
renv::update()

# Check status
renv::status()
```

## Session Information

```{r}
# Always include session info in reports
sessionInfo()

# Or with devtools
library(devtools)
session_info()
```

## Docker for R

```dockerfile
FROM rocker/tidyverse:4.3.0

# Install additional packages
RUN R -e "install.packages('package_name')"

# Copy project files
COPY . /home/rstudio/project

# Set working directory
WORKDIR /home/rstudio/project
```

# 8. Data Management

## Data Organization

```{r eval=FALSE}
# Keep raw data untouched
raw_data <- read.csv(here("data", "raw", "original_data.csv"))

# Save processed data
processed_data <- clean_data(raw_data)
saveRDS(processed_data, here("data", "processed", "clean_data.rds"))

# Document data processing
# Keep script: scripts/01_data_processing.R
```

## Data Documentation

```{r eval=FALSE}
# Create data dictionary
data_dictionary <- data.frame(
  Variable = names(dataset),
  Description = c("Patient ID", "Age in years", ...),
  Type = c("character", "numeric", ...),
  Values = c("Unique ID", "18-90", ...)
)

write.csv(data_dictionary, here("docs", "data_dictionary.csv"))
```

## Checksums for Data Integrity

```{r eval=FALSE}
# Calculate MD5 checksum
tools::md5sum(here("data", "raw", "data.csv"))

# Verify data hasn't changed
original_md5 <- "abc123..."
current_md5 <- tools::md5sum(here("data", "raw", "data.csv"))
identical(original_md5, current_md5)
```

# 9. Literate Programming Best Practices

## Code Organization in Notebooks

```{r eval=FALSE}
# 1. Setup chunk (packages, options)
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE)

# 2. Load data
data <- read.csv(here("data", "data.csv"))

# 3. Explore data
glimpse(data)

# 4. Clean data
clean_data <- data %>% filter(!is.na(value))

# 5. Analyze
results <- analyze(clean_data)

# 6. Visualize
ggplot(results, aes(x, y)) + geom_point()

# 7. Save outputs
saveRDS(results, here("output", "results.rds"))
```

## Comments and Documentation

```{r eval=FALSE}
# Good comments explain WHY, not WHAT
# Bad:
x <- x + 1  # Add 1 to x

# Good:
x <- x + 1  # Adjust for 1-based indexing in output

# Document functions
#' Calculate summary statistics
#'
#' @param data A numeric vector
#' @param na.rm Logical, remove NAs?
#' @return A named vector of statistics
#' @examples
#' calc_stats(c(1, 2, 3, NA), na.rm = TRUE)
calc_stats <- function(data, na.rm = FALSE) {
  c(mean = mean(data, na.rm = na.rm),
    sd = sd(data, na.rm = na.rm))
}
```

## Notebook Template

```markdown
---
title: "Analysis Title"
author: "Author Name"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: html_document
---

```

# 10. Automated Reporting

## Parameterized Reports

```{r eval=FALSE}
# Create reports for multiple conditions
species_list <- c("setosa", "versicolor", "virginica")

for (sp in species_list) {
  rmarkdown::render(
    "species_report.Rmd",
    params = list(species = sp),
    output_file = paste0("report_", sp, ".html")
  )
}
```

## Scheduled Reports

```{r eval=FALSE}
# Use cronR or taskscheduleR for scheduling

# Linux/Mac (cron)
library(cronR)
cmd <- cron_rscript("weekly_report.R")
cron_add(cmd, frequency = "weekly", id = "weekly_report")

# Windows (Task Scheduler)
library(taskscheduleR)
taskscheduler_create(taskname = "weekly_report",
                     rscript = "weekly_report.R",
                     schedule = "WEEKLY")
```

## Email Reports

```{r eval=FALSE}
library(blastula)

# Create email
email <- render_email("report.Rmd")

# Send email
smtp_send(
  email,
  from = "sender@example.com",
  to = "recipient@example.com",
  subject = "Weekly Report",
  credentials = creds_file("email_creds")
)
```

# 11. Testing and Validation

## testthat Package

```{r eval=FALSE}
library(testthat)

# Write tests
test_that("mean calculation works", {
  expect_equal(mean(c(1, 2, 3)), 2)
  expect_true(mean(c(1, 2, 3)) > 0)
  expect_error(mean("not numeric"))
})

# Test file structure
test_that("data has expected columns", {
  expect_true("Species" %in% names(iris))
  expect_equal(ncol(iris), 5)
})

# Run all tests
test_dir("tests/")
```

## Assertions

```{r eval=FALSE}
library(assertthat)

# Validate assumptions
assert_that(is.numeric(data$value))
assert_that(all(data$age >= 0))
assert_that(length(unique(data$id)) == nrow(data))
```

# 12. Collaboration and Sharing

## GitHub for Collaboration

```bash
# Fork repository on GitHub
# Clone your fork
git clone https://github.com/yourusername/repo.git

# Add upstream remote
git remote add upstream https://github.com/original/repo.git

# Sync with upstream
git fetch upstream
git merge upstream/main

# Create pull request
git checkout -b feature-branch
# Make changes
git add .
git commit -m "Add feature"
git push origin feature-branch
# Create PR on GitHub
```

## Code Review

- Clear commit messages
- Small, focused pull requests
- Document changes
- Add tests
- Request reviews

```

# 14. Reproducibility Checklist

- [ ] Code is version controlled
- [ ] Dependencies are documented (renv)
- [ ] Raw data is preserved and documented
- [ ] Analysis is documented (R Markdown)
- [ ] Code is tested
- [ ] Session information is included
- [ ] README with instructions
- [ ] Clear file organization
- [ ] Appropriate license
- [ ] Data and code are backed up
- [ ] Results can be reproduced
